question_text:
A 27-year-old G1P0 at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents for prenatal care. The patient says she has occasional nausea and vomiting and a few episodes of palpitations and diarrhea this last week. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for a heart rate of 145/min. Basic thyroid function tests are shown in the table below. Which of the following additional laboratory tests would be most useful is assessing this patient’s condition?
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 
0.28 mIU/L (0.3–4.5 mIU/L)
Total T4
12 µg/dL (5.4–11.5 µg/dL)?

        ### Question
        A 27-year-old G1P0 at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents for prenatal care. The patient says she has occasional nausea and vomiting and a few episodes of palpitations and diarrhea this last week. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for a heart rate of 145/min. Basic thyroid function tests are shown in the table below. Which of the following additional laboratory tests would be most useful is assessing this patient’s condition?
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 
0.28 mIU/L (0.3–4.5 mIU/L)
Total T4
12 µg/dL (5.4–11.5 µg/dL)?

        ### Options
        opa. Total triiodothyronine (T3) levels
opb. Free thyroxine (T4) levels
opc. Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) levels
opd. Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies
ope. Thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb)

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Patient presents with nausea, vomiting, palpitations, and diarrhea" -> "Heart rate of 145/min indicates possible hyperthyroidism" -> "TSH level is low at 0.28 mIU/L" -> "Total T4 level is elevated at 12 µg/dL" -> "Suggests hyperthyroidism" -> "Free T4 levels would help assess thyroid function more accurately" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Patient has symptoms consistent with hyperthyroidism" -> "Low TSH and elevated Total T4 confirm thyroid dysfunction" -> "Need to determine the active form of thyroid hormone" -> "Free T4 levels provide a clearer picture of thyroid status" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Elevated Total T4 suggests increased thyroid hormone production" -> "Low TSH indicates feedback suppression" -> "Free T4 levels would clarify the degree of hyperthyroidism" -> "Other tests like T3 or TPO antibodies are less relevant at this stage" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Symptoms and lab results suggest hyperthyroidism" -> "Free T4 levels are critical for diagnosis" -> "Total T3 levels may also be informative but less critical" -> "Free T4 is the most direct measure of thyroid hormone activity" -> 88%
